examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Tuple relational calculus specifies conditions rather than an operator plan. Existential quantification expresses a witness; universal quantification often becomes 'no violating witness exists'. Free tuple variables determine output attributes. Unrestricted negation can range over an infinite domain, so safe/domain-independent expressions constrain outputs to values derived from the database. Logical equivalence must preserve quantifier scope.

**Key relationship:** {t | R(t) ∧ predicate(t)} describes tuples satisfying a formula

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify free and bound variables.
2. Rewrite universal claims as no counterexample.
3. Check output variables are range-restricted.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Bind every tuple variable to its relation and explicitly equate the components representing shared values. Existential witnesses express that a matching tuple exists; they do not automatically impose a join. Safe/range-restricted queries return values drawn from a finite active domain rather than arbitrary elements of an unbounded universe.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
R={(1,4),(2,4),(3,5)}, S={(4,9)}. How many distinct u satisfy ∃v,w [(u,v)∈R AND (v,w)∈S]?

**Answer: 2.** The shared v must be 4 from S's first component. R then permits u=1 or 2. The projected result has two distinct values. u=3 has v=5 and no S witness.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A universal quantifier does not mean existence. In particular a universal condition can be vacuously true over an empty set of witnesses.

Negation must not introduce an unbounded set of arbitrary domain values.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A safe query should avoid:

- **A.** Unbounded output over values unrelated to the finite database
- **B.** Any conjunction
- **C.** All relation predicates
- **D.** All quantifiers

**Answer: A.** Safety prevents expressions such as outputting every tuple not in a relation over an unbounded domain.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Existential quantifiers express witnesses
- **B.** Universal conditions can be rewritten using negated existence
- **C.** Free variables may describe output
- **D.** Every syntactically valid expression is safe

**Answer: A, B, C.** Syntax alone does not ensure finite domain-independent output.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

R has three distinct one-attribute tuples. How many tuples satisfy {t | R(t)}?



**Answer: 3.** The relation predicate restricts t exactly to the three existing R tuples; no extra domain values enter.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q39 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/tuple-calculus?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Tuple relational calculus and safety. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. The result must project pname from a tuple p in players, not from teams. That eliminates B,D.
2. A player qualifies only when there exists a team tuple t with p.tid=t.tid and t.tname='MI'. A includes both this join condition and the name condition.
3. C merely asserts that an MI team exists and would admit unrelated players. The correct query is **A**.

#### GATE 2026 CS1 · Q43 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/tuple-calculus?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Tuple relational calculus and safety. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. In the calculus expression, tuple (u,v) belongs to R, so u corresponds to R.P and v to R.Q. Tuple (v,w) belongs to S, so the same v corresponds to S.X.
2. Join on R.Q=S.X, then project R.P. The order of the join operands does not change that condition.
3. This matches **B**.
